answer.diagnosis: Layer-1 unit 19 is the odd one out. Its weights are uniformly positive (about 15 to 90) over the entire 24x24 grid: all four corners, the borders and the background. It has no centre-versus-ring structure and is, if anything, slightly lower at the blob centre (r11-r12, c12). So it simply sums the brightness of the whole image, and its output is dominated by background intensity rather than by how big the blob is. The other trained units are structured size detectors. Units 1, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30 respond positively to a ring at radius about 5-8, which suits large blobs. Units 0, 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28 and 31 respond to a bright centre with a dark ring, which suits small blobs. The remaining units look like untrained noise. Unit 19 feeds strongly into layer-2 units that carry large output weights (u13 +69 then +95 to the logit, u15 +68 then +63, u12 +43, u9 +39, u0 +36). This indicates the model partly uses global image or background brightness as a cue that was correlated with the label. That is a shortcut, not blob size. This conclusion rests only on the weight pattern, so it is moderately uncertain; whole-image brightness does also grow somewhat with blob size. Fix: cut unit 19's outgoing connections (W2 column 19) so global brightness no longer reaches the decision. The size information carried by the structured centre and ring units is left intact. Downstream biases were not recalibrated, because the typical activation of unit 19 cannot be known from the weights alone.
